data: What is the difference between two consecutive tick values on the y axis?

The y-axis represents density, and the x-axis represents standard deviation. The y-axis has a range from 0.0 to approximately 1.7. The y-axis has evenly spaced tick marks. The difference between two consecutive tick values can be calculated by dividing the total range of the y-axis by the number of intervals between the tick marks. There are 5 visible tick marks on the y-axis, which means there are 4 intervals between them. Therefore, the difference between two consecutive tick values is approximately 1.7 / 4 = 0.425.
